senses.meaning: Thuộc ngoại giao; khéo léo trong giao tiếp, tế nhị
examples: He accused the ambassador of diplomatic double-talk.
They have established diplomatic relations with many countries.
Her diplomatic response avoided offending either side.

senses.meaning: Lệnh cấm vận (cấm thương mại hoặc giao thương với một quốc gia/tổ chức)
examples: Many allies are pushing to lift the trade embargo.
During the war, they laid an embargo on commerce with enemy countries.
The arms embargo was extended for another year.

senses.meaning: Áp đặt lệnh cấm vận
examples: The Security Council voted to embargo oil exports.
Several nations moved to embargo the regime's assets.
They threatened to embargo imports from the country.

senses.meaning: Thăm dò ý kiến cử tri ngay sau khi bỏ phiếu (để dự đoán kết quả bầu cử)
examples: Exit polls predicted a very close race.
The exit poll was wrong: the actual result differed by ten points.
National exit polls showed 54 percent of women voted for the incumbent.

note: Khác với 'opinion poll' (thăm dò trước bầu cử): exit poll được thực hiện ngay khi người dân rời khỏi phòng bỏ phiếu.

senses.meaning: Người theo đường lối cứng rắn, không chịu thỏa hiệp
examples: He needs to persuade the hard-liners in the cabinet to accept the deal.
Hardliners in the party blocked any reform for years.
The hardliner faction gained influence after the election.

senses.meaning: Uỷ nhiệm, quyền được trao (thường do bầu cử); nhiệm vụ được giao
examples: The President had a clear mandate to end the war.
She was elected with a strong mandate to tackle corruption.
The UN mandate authorised peacekeepers to use force if necessary.

senses.meaning: Ra lệnh, uỷ nhiệm (chính thức)
examples: The constitution mandates a general election every five years.
New regulations mandate the use of safety equipment on all sites.
The court mandated the release of all political prisoners.

senses.meaning: Hiệp ước, thỏa thuận (thường có tính ràng buộc)
examples: The two countries signed a non-aggression pact.
He made a pact with his colleagues not to discuss salaries.
The peace pact collapsed after the border incident.

senses.meaning: Sự đàn áp (chính trị); sự kìm nén (cảm xúc)
examples: The political repression in this country is enforced by terror.
They suffered years of repression at the hands of the old regime.
Psychological repression of traumatic memories can have long-term effects.

senses.meaning: Lệnh trừng phạt (quốc tế); sự phê chuẩn/chấp thuận
examples: Economic sanctions were imposed on the regime.
Their ideas received official sanction at the UN meeting.
Prison is the ultimate sanction of the legal system.

senses.meaning: Chấp thuận, phê chuẩn chính thức
examples: The church refused to sanction the king's second marriage.
The committee sanctioned the use of emergency funds.
The project was sanctioned by the board after months of review.

note: Hai nghĩa trái ngược: (1) trừng phạt; (2) chấp thuận. Xem ngữ cảnh để phân biệt.

senses.meaning: Chủ quyền (quyền tự quyết tối cao của một quốc gia)
examples: The country claimed sovereignty over the disputed island.
China exercises sovereignty over Hong Kong.
National sovereignty must be respected under international law.

senses.meaning: Hiệp ước, điều ước quốc tế (văn kiện ký kết giữa các quốc gia)
examples: The two nations signed a peace treaty after years of conflict.
The treaty was declared invalid because it had not been ratified.
The Nuclear Non-Proliferation Treaty aims to prevent the spread of nuclear weapons.

senses.meaning: Kho bạc nhà nước, ngân khố; Bộ Tài chính
examples: The Treasury announced new measures to reduce the deficit.
America's Treasury Secretary identified the most heavily indebted countries.
The national treasury was depleted by years of conflict.

note: Viết hoa khi chỉ cơ quan/bộ cụ thể: 'the Treasury'.

senses.meaning: Toàn vẹn lãnh thổ (nguyên tắc trong luật quốc tế)
examples: The nation vowed to defend its territorial integrity at all costs.
Respecting territorial integrity is a cornerstone of the UN Charter.
The conflict threatened the territorial integrity of the entire region.

note: Cụm từ quan trọng trong ngoại giao và luật quốc tế.

senses.meaning: Lật đổ (chính quyền, người cầm quyền); ngã đổ
examples: Political corruption threatened to topple the regime.
The coup toppled the democratically elected government.
The stack of books toppled off the shelf.

senses.meaning: Chế độ độc tài
examples: The generals established a military dictatorship after the coup.
The country suffered under dictatorship for thirty years.
His dictatorship was marked by the suppression of free speech.

senses.meaning: Nhà độc tài
examples: The dictator ruled the country with an iron fist.
History has shown that dictators eventually fall from power.
The people rose up against the dictator after decades of oppression.

senses.meaning: Độc đoán, độc tài
examples: His attitude became increasingly dictatorial as his power grew.
He suspended the constitution and assumed dictatorial powers.
Her dictatorial management style drove away talented staff.

senses.meaning: Trợ cấp (tiền nhà nước hỗ trợ cho ngành/cá nhân)
examples: The government cut agricultural subsidies to reduce the deficit.
The banks received a government subsidy to cover the interest rate differential.
Farm subsidies are controversial in international trade negotiations.

senses.meaning: Thuộc về Quốc hội (đặc biệt là Quốc hội Mỹ)
examples: The president explained his plans to congressional leaders.
A congressional hearing was scheduled to investigate the scandal.
Congressional approval is required for any declaration of war.

note: Chủ yếu dùng với Quốc hội Mỹ (Congress). Quốc hội Anh dùng 'parliamentary'.

senses.meaning: Sắc lệnh, nghị định (lệnh chính thức từ người có quyền)
examples: The Emperor issued a decree repealing martial law.
An official decree invalidated the vote in the capital.
The decree was published in the official gazette.

senses.meaning: Ra sắc lệnh, ban lệnh
examples: The president decreed that all schools would reopen on Monday.
The court decreed that the contract was null and void.
The king decreed a national holiday to celebrate the victory.

senses.meaning: Người biểu tình; người trình diễn (sản phẩm)
examples: As he left the meeting, he was berated by angry demonstrators.
Thousands of demonstrators marched through the city centre.
She worked as a product demonstrator at trade fairs.

senses.meaning: Quyền bầu cử
examples: Suffrage demands by women became increasingly vocal in the early 20th century.
Universal suffrage was achieved after decades of campaigning.
The suffrage movement changed the course of democracy worldwide.

note: 'Universal suffrage' = phổ thông đầu phiếu. The Suffragettes were British women who campaigned for the right to vote.

senses.meaning: Chủ nghĩa đế quốc (chính sách mở rộng lãnh thổ và ảnh hưởng)
examples: Plunder is the very nature of imperialism.
Critics accuse tech giants of cultural imperialism.
The book traces the rise and fall of European imperialism.

senses.meaning: Quá khích, thiếu kiềm chế (ngôn từ hoặc hành vi)
examples: The tone of the minister's article was intemperate.
His intemperate remarks during the interview caused a public backlash.
The governor refused to be provoked into intemperate action.

senses.meaning: Kẻ nổi loạn, chiến binh vũ trang nổi dậy chống chính quyền
examples: Several insurgents were captured in the border crackdown.
The army battled insurgents in the mountain regions for months.
A suspected insurgent was arrested inside his home.

senses.meaning: Có tính nổi loạn, thuộc phong trào nổi dậy
examples: Insurgent forces were reported advancing in the region.
The insurgent movement grew in strength after the economic collapse.
Insurgent groups used the remote valleys as hideouts.

senses.meaning: Chủ nghĩa khủng bố (dùng bạo lực hoặc đe dọa vì mục đích chính trị)
examples: The government declared war on terrorism after the attack.
International cooperation is essential in the fight against terrorism.
The legislation criminalised the financing of terrorism.

senses.meaning: Bạo chúa, kẻ cai trị tàn ác
examples: The tyrant ruled through fear and intimidation.
History remembers him as a cruel tyrant who silenced all dissent.
The people rose up and overthrew the tyrant.

senses.meaning: Lãnh thổ; vùng đất thuộc phạm vi kiểm soát; lĩnh vực
examples: The army recaptured the territory lost in the first battle.
Negotiations over disputed territory continued for months.
This topic is uncharted territory for the committee.

senses.meaning: Áp bức, khắc nghiệt; ngột ngạt (thời tiết hoặc cảm giác)
examples: The new laws are just as oppressive as those they replace.
The political situation has grown increasingly oppressive.
The oppressive August heat made it hard to breathe.

senses.meaning: Người theo chủ nghĩa dân túy (tuyên bố đại diện cho 'người dân thường' chống lại 'giới tinh hoa')
examples: Populists have gained ground in many democracies in recent years.
The populist promised to drain the swamp and return power to the people.
Critics accused the leader of being a dangerous populist.

senses.meaning: Thuộc chủ nghĩa dân túy, mang tính dân túy
examples: The candidate adopted a populist platform to appeal to working-class voters.
Populist rhetoric often oversimplifies complex political issues.
The movement's populist appeal cut across traditional party lines.

note: 'Populism' thường mang hàm ý tiêu cực trong báo chí phương Tây — ngụ ý đơn giản hóa vấn đề phức tạp.

senses.meaning: Giai cấp vô sản (giai cấp công nhân không có tư liệu sản xuất)
examples: Marx believed the proletariat would eventually overthrow the bourgeoisie.
The revolution was led by the urban proletariat.
The party claimed to represent the interests of the proletariat.

note: Thuật ngữ Marxist. Đối lập với 'bourgeoisie' (giai cấp tư sản).

senses.meaning: Tước vị quý tộc (trong hệ thống Anh: công, hầu, bá, tử, nam); giới quý tộc
examples: The Prime Minister offered him a life peerage for his services.
Prior to union, each kingdom had its own peerage.
Sir Peter was raised to the peerage with the title of Baron.

note: Hệ thống quý tộc Anh gồm 5 cấp: Duke, Marquess, Earl, Viscount, Baron.

senses.meaning: Phê chuẩn, thông qua chính thức (hiệp ước, luật, hay thỏa thuận)
examples: The treaty was ratified by all member states.
Congress ratified the amendment after a lengthy debate.
The agreement will not take effect until both sides ratify it.

senses.meaning: Chế độ, chính quyền (thường ám chỉ chính quyền độc đoán hoặc chuyên quyền)
examples: The authoritarian regime silenced all opposition.
A new regime took power following the coup.
The old regime collapsed under the weight of popular protest.

note: 'Regime' thường hàm ý tiêu cực; để trung lập hơn dùng 'government' hoặc 'administration'.

senses.meaning: Cuộc nổi loạn, nổi dậy (chống lại chính quyền hoặc quyền lực)
examples: The peasants rose in revolt against the king's taxes.
The revolt was crushed within a week by loyalist forces.
A palace revolt ousted the prime minister from within her own party.

senses.meaning: Nổi loạn; gây kinh tởm, ghê tởm
examples: The people revolted against the unjust laws.
Several MPs revolted against the government's tax bill.
The graphic scenes revolted even seasoned journalists.

note: Hai nghĩa: (1) chính trị: nổi loạn; (2) cảm xúc: gây phản cảm/ghê tởm.

senses.meaning: Trưng cầu dân ý
examples: The country held a referendum on independence.
Citizens voted in the referendum after months of intense campaigning.
The referendum result surprised most political analysts.

note: Số nhiều: 'referendums' (thông thường) hoặc 'referenda' (học thuật). 'Plebiscite' = trưng cầu dân ý không ràng buộc pháp lý.

senses.meaning: Cuộc nổi dậy, chống đối (thường có tổ chức, có thể vũ trang)
examples: The rebellion was swiftly crushed by the military.
A spirit of rebellion ran through the youth movement.
The rebellion against the regime lasted three years before being suppressed.

senses.meaning: Sự trỗi dậy, hồi sinh (của phong trào, xu hướng, hay thế lực)
examples: There has been a resurgence of interest in traditional crafts.
The resurgence of nationalism alarmed neighbouring countries.
Economic resurgence followed years of stagnation.

senses.meaning: Chủ nghĩa cấp tiến; chủ nghĩa cực đoan chính trị
examples: Radicalism in politics can destabilise the status quo.
The rise of radicalism alarmed moderate politicians.
Economic inequality often fuels the spread of radicalism.

senses.meaning: Âm mưu (bí mật bàn tính làm điều xấu); thuyết âm mưu
examples: They were convicted of conspiracy to commit fraud.
The conspiracy theory was dismissed as baseless by the authorities.
A conspiracy within the party nearly brought down the government.

senses.meaning: Liên minh (chính trị, giữa các đảng hoặc quốc gia)
examples: The two parties formed a coalition government after neither won a majority.
The international coalition launched a joint military operation.
Coalition politics requires compromise from all sides.

senses.meaning: Thoái vị (vua chúa); từ bỏ trách nhiệm
examples: The king abdicated in favour of his eldest son.
Leaders should not abdicate their responsibility to act in a crisis.
He abdicated his role as team leader under pressure.

senses.meaning: Xóa bỏ, bãi bỏ (luật, tập tục, hay tổ chức) hoàn toàn
examples: Slavery was abolished in Britain in 1833.
The new government promised to abolish the unpopular bedroom tax.
Some argue that the death penalty should be abolished globally.

senses.meaning: Quyền tự trị (quyền quản lý nội bộ độc lập)
examples: The region was granted limited autonomy over its domestic affairs.
Teachers need more autonomy in the classroom.
The university enjoys considerable autonomy from the government.

senses.meaning: Lòng trung thành (với quốc gia, đảng phái, hay tổ chức)
examples: He pledged allegiance to the new government.
Her allegiance to the party never wavered throughout her career.
The soldiers swore an oath of allegiance to the Crown.

note: 'Pledge allegiance' = tuyên thệ trung thành. The Pledge of Allegiance là lời thề của người Mỹ với quốc kỳ.

senses.meaning: Tối hậu thư (đòi hỏi cuối cùng, nếu không chấp nhận sẽ có hậu quả)
examples: He issued an ultimatum: accept the terms or face military action.
The government rejected the ultimatum from the rebel group.
Issuing ultimatums rarely leads to productive negotiation.

note: Số nhiều: 'ultimatums' (thông thường) hoặc 'ultimata' (học thuật).

senses.meaning: Thuộc địa hoá, thiết lập thuộc địa; chiếm đóng (nghĩa bóng)
examples: European powers colonised much of Africa and Asia during the 19th century.
The island was colonised by Dutch settlers in the 17th century.
Companies are beginning to colonise digital spaces in new ways.

note: Tiếng Anh Mỹ: 'colonize'.

senses.meaning: Sự đề cử (ứng viên, giải thưởng, chức vụ)
examples: Her nomination for the Booker Prize was widely praised.
The party announced its presidential nomination at the convention.
He accepted the nomination with a short but heartfelt speech.

senses.meaning: Tiểu vương quốc (do emir cai trị)
examples: The emirate opened parts of its property market to foreign buyers.
The United Arab Emirates is a federation of seven emirates.
The emirate invested heavily in infrastructure and tourism.

senses.meaning: Người theo chủ nghĩa nữ quyền
examples: All her life she was an ardent feminist.
Prominent feminists gathered for the conference on gender equality.
He called himself a feminist and championed equal pay legislation.

senses.meaning: Thuộc chủ nghĩa nữ quyền
examples: She wrote from a firmly feminist perspective.
The novel has been praised for its feminist themes.
Feminist theory challenges traditional power structures in society.

senses.meaning: Chế độ nô lệ; tình trạng bị buộc phải làm việc khổ sai
examples: William Wilberforce campaigned for the abolition of slavery.
People are still suffering under the yoke of modern slavery.
They condemned slavery as the gravest violation of human rights.

note: 'Modern slavery' = nô lệ hiện đại: cưỡng bức lao động, buôn người.

senses.meaning: Một cách dân chủ
examples: This committee will enable decisions to be made democratically.
They saw their democratically elected president overthrown by a military coup.
The motion was democratically put to a vote.

senses.meaning: Cơ quan lập pháp (quốc hội, nghị viện)
examples: The legislature passed a new bill on environmental protection.
They voted to reduce the power of the legislature.
The bill was sent to the legislature for approval.

senses.meaning: Cử tri, toàn thể cử tri
examples: According to polls, the British electorate is deeply divided.
There is widespread apathy among the electorate this election cycle.
Only about half of the electorate bothered to vote.

senses.meaning: Kháng nghị ngoại giao (tuyên bố hoặc yêu cầu chính thức qua kênh ngoại giao)
examples: The US government issued a demarche to protest the new trade restrictions.
The embassy delivered a demarche requesting the release of detained citizens.
A diplomatic demarche was filed after the spy expulsions.

note: Từ tiếng Pháp. Formal diplomatic term.

senses.meaning: Phong kiến (thuộc chế độ phong kiến)
examples: The feudal system was based on land ownership and vassalage.
Public opinion was firmly against preserving the old feudal order.
They were hired as soldiers by feudal lords in exchange for land.

senses.meaning: Đơn phương (do một phía quyết định, không có sự đồng thuận của bên kia)
examples: The rebels unilaterally declared a ceasefire.
The district unilaterally proclaimed its independence.
The country cannot unilaterally withdraw from an international treaty.

note: Phân biệt: 'bilaterally' (song phương), 'multilaterally' (đa phương).

senses.meaning: Tước quyền bầu cử; tước đoạt quyền lợi cơ bản
examples: Voter suppression laws effectively disenfranchise minority communities.
Those without a fixed address are often disenfranchised.
The ruling disenfranchised millions of citizens living abroad.

note: Ngược lại: 'enfranchise' = trao quyền bầu cử.

senses.meaning: Tước bỏ quyền lực, làm mất tiếng nói
examples: Centralising all decisions disempowers regional governments.
The media can disempower citizens by keeping them ill-informed.
Structural inequality systematically disempowers marginalised groups.

senses.meaning: Ngoại giao; kỹ năng xử lý tế nhị trong quan hệ cá nhân
examples: Economic diplomacy has become as important as military power.
The two leaders resolved the crisis through quiet diplomacy.
It took great diplomacy to keep all parties at the negotiating table.

senses.meaning: Sự ngoan cố, không chịu nhượng bộ hay thỏa hiệp
examples: Political intransigence on both sides blocked any meaningful progress.
The prime minister's intransigence over treaty terms shocked allies.
Voters grew frustrated with the intransigence of the ruling coalition.

note: Từ gốc: 'intransigent' (adj) = cứng đầu, không chịu thỏa hiệp.

senses.meaning: Hối lộ (tiền hoặc vật phẩm đưa để mua chuộc)
examples: The official was convicted of accepting a bribe.
He tried to pay a bribe to avoid prosecution.
Bribery and corruption are widespread problems in some administrations.

senses.meaning: Hối lộ, mua chuộc
examples: He tried to bribe the inspector to overlook the violations.
She was accused of bribing officials to secure the contract.
The witness was bribed into changing his testimony.

senses.meaning: Quyền tị nạn chính trị; nơi tị nạn; (lịch sử) bệnh viện tâm thần
examples: The opposition leader sought asylum in a neighbouring country.
Asylum seekers must demonstrate a well-founded fear of persecution.
The government's asylum policy drew criticism from human rights groups.

note: 'Seek/claim asylum' = xin tị nạn. Nghĩa lịch sử: nơi trú ẩn cho người tâm thần.

senses.meaning: Thuộc về hàng hải, biển; gần biển
examples: The nation asserted its maritime rights in the disputed zone.
Maritime borders are governed by the UN Convention on the Law of the Sea.
Britain's maritime heritage includes centuries of naval dominance.
